Authors: Epp, A.M., & Humphreys, A.
Title: Collaborating with Generative AI in Consumer Culture Research
Why It Matters: CONFIRMED 2026-08-13 (read in full): the strongest anchor available, and now the recommended OPENING citation for any methods section doing AI-assisted thematic/qualitative analysis, ahead of Berger et al. 2020. JCR (top-3 marketing journal, the home journal for qualitative/consumer-culture work specifically), built from interviews with researchers actually using GenAI on qualitative textual data, and supplies a ready-made 4-principle reporting checklist (transparency, provenance, privacy, verisimilitude). Already being cited/followed by Pueschel, Hao & Schmitt 2026.

Journal/Venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services, 88, 104520

Authors: Pueschel, J., Hao, S., & Schmitt, B.
Title: Understanding Luxury Shaming: A Multi-Study Exploration Using Qualitative Inquiry and Generative AI
Why It Matters: CONFIRMED 2026-08-13 (read in full): closest methodological cousin to the Tariff/CCS/Data Center papers' Study 1 design - manual NVivo thematic analysis run in parallel with GenAI (NotebookLM/ChatGPT) analysis, then axial coding to reconcile, explicitly following Epp & Humphreys' (2025) guidelines. Applied JBR precedent, directly citable as 'following the protocol of.'

Authors: Hill, C., Dahil, A., Simpson, G., Hardisty, D., Keast, J., Pinn, C.K., & Dambha-Miller, H.
Title: Large Language Models for Thematic Analysis in Healthcare Research: A Blinded Mixed-Methods Comparison with Human Analysts
Why It Matters: Blinded quantified agreement stats (93.5% deductive agreement, Gwet's AC1=0.93) against human coders, specifically using Claude 4 Sonnet. Good numbers for a reviewer.

Authors: AlGhamdi, R.
Title: From Code Variability to Theme Convergence: AI-Human Alignment in Thematic Analysis With Claude Code
Why It Matters: Only paper validating Claude Code specifically (not just chat-based Claude) against a human/NVivo baseline. Open access - full PDF verified 2026-08-13 via Ole Miss library: 4 independent Claude Code sessions (2 general prompts, 2 structured multi-phase) vs. original 2012 NVivo human analysis of 16 interviews. Key finding for citing - hierarchical convergence: code-level F1 varies widely (55.9-87.6%, structured prompting beats general 83.1% vs 59.2%) but theme-level F1 stays high and stable (90.9-100%) with strong inter-session consistency (86.1% avg). Also reports 100% quote-verification accuracy (0 fabrications across 64 sampled quotes) vs. 42% for Microsoft Copilot in a comparable study - strong citable contrast. Saved to Claude Knowledge/Thematic Analysis/.

Title: Human-AI Collaborative Inductive Thematic Analysis: How AI Guides Analysis and Researchers Reclaim Interpretive Authority

Authors: Paulus, T., Lester, J.N., & Davis, C.
Title: The Construction of the Role of AI in Qualitative Data Analysis in the Social Sciences
Why It Matters: CONFIRMED 2026-08-13 (read in full): discourse analysis of 29 published articles' own framing of AI's role in QDA, identifying 5 stances: (1) QDA is inherently problematic, (2) QDA will inevitably be automated, (3) AI disrupts without replacing humans, (4) AI-human hybrid methods are the future, (5) de-centering ethics/limitations. New section added to Study1_AI_Thematic_Analysis_Publishable_Protocol.md recommending stance 4 as the one to write into - matches this protocol's existing six-phase engine.

Authors: Nguyen-Trung, K.
Title: (same paper as above - Tier 2 entry)
Why It Matters: Represents the Braun & Clarke 'Big Q' objection - reflexive TA's point is researcher subjectivity, and AI 'systematic/reduce-bias' framing is methodologically incongruent. A reviewer trained in reflexive TA may raise exactly this - address head-on in methods, don't get blindsided.

Authors: Karhu, K., Smolander, K., & Kasurinen, J.
Title: To Vibe Research or Not to Vibe Research? Generative AI in Qualitative Research
Why It Matters: CORRECTED authors vs. prior placeholder entry. Full text read 2026-08-13: sharper version of the opposition than Nguyen-Trung alone. Uses the same small-q/Big-Q split this protocol already uses. Three specific objections: (1) methodological incongruence (using inter-rater reliability, a small-q metric, inside a Big-Q/reflexive design), (2) AI cannot be reflexive, (3) AI supply-chain ethics (environmental + labor cost, citing Miceli et al. 2025) treated as first-order not an afterthought. Cites the 419-researcher Jowsey et al. 2025 rejection statement - see that row below.

Title: We Reject the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence for Reflexive Qualitative Research
Journal/Venue: Qualitative Inquiry, e-pub ahead of print 2025-12-17
Why It Matters: VERIFIED 2026-08-16: real DOI confirmed (10.1177/10778004251401851), CC BY 4.0 open-access license (so a legally free copy should exist somewhere despite the SAGE-page 403 hit this pass - worth one more direct-fetch attempt, e.g. via the KCL PURE repository's own PDF link, before assuming it needs an Ole Miss pull). Authors: De Paoli, S.
Title: Why We Should Reject to Reject the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Qualitative Analysis: A Response to Jowsey, Braun, Clarke, Lupton, and Fine (2025)
Why It Matters: NEW ROW, added 2026-08-16. Direct, real, published rebuttal to the Jowsey et al. 2025 rejection statement above - confirmed real via WebSearch/WebFetch (Abertay University repository page). Argues the Jowsey et al. objections, while framed as methodological, largely rest on philosophical assumptions risking dogma; calls for continued scrutiny and rigor but not categorical rejection, framing engagement with GenAI tools as compatible with reflexivity if done openly and collaboratively. Strategically valuable: citing this alongside Jowsey et al. lets a methods section acknowledge the strongest opposition citation available while also showing the field itself is actively contesting it, not settled against AI-assisted qualitative work.
